## Overview {#sec-targets}

This chapter is the deliverable section — where multi-layer evidence converges into a ranked shortlist of overexpression (OE) and knockout (KO) candidates for experimental validation.

::: {.callout-warning}
**To Revisit:** The overexpression and knockout candidate scoring criteria below reflect the current framework. These criteria — particularly the evidence-weighting and ranking methodology — will be updated once the final scoring framework is agreed in the team review. Check with Arjun / Yogesh before using these criteria for final experimental planning.
:::

---

## What Makes a High-Confidence Candidate?

The KG scores candidates across six dimensions:

```{=html}
<div class="step-box"><div class="step-number">1</div><div><strong>Direction and Strength of Association</strong> — Spearman correlation of gene/protein/metabolite abundance with qP, titre, IVCD (<code>correlation_factor</code> on the <code>positive</code>/<code>negative</code> edge)</div></div>
<div class="step-box"><div class="step-number">2</div><div><strong>Multi-Omics Signal</strong> — Concordant DE at both RNA and protein level (directional consistency: mRNA up and protein up, or both down)</div></div>
<div class="step-box"><div class="step-number">3</div><div><strong>Consensus Signal</strong> — Agreement across DEG, WGCNA module membership, and MOFA Factor loading</div></div>
<div class="step-box"><div class="step-number">4</div><div><strong>Pathway / Functional Role</strong> — Target involved in productivity-relevant biology (secretory pathway, ER stress, metabolic flux)</div></div>
<div class="step-box"><div class="step-number">5</div><div><strong>Impact on Growth and Titer</strong> — In-silico GEM perturbation predicting effects on secretion with minimal growth penalty <em>(in progress — not yet in KG)</em></div></div>
<div class="step-box"><div class="step-number">6</div><div><strong>Causal Mining Evidence</strong> — Publication-evidence score from curated genetic manipulation studies (<code>causal_weight</code> on literature edges)</div></div>
```

---

## Overexpression Candidates

Genes expected to **increase** productivity when expressed at higher levels.

**Criteria:**

- Upregulated in high producers in ≥7/10 BMS Study 1 cohorts
- Positive Spearman correlation with qP (r > 0.5)
- Positive MOFA Factor 1 weight
- Member of a pro-productivity WGCNA network
- Published OE evidence showing positive productivity effect (where available)

::: {.query-box}
Identify overexpression candidates: genes upregulated in high producers across ≥7/10 Study 1 cohorts, with positive MOFA Factor 1 weight and positive qP correlation > 0.5.
:::

::: {.query-box}
Rank overexpression candidates by number of supporting high-producer cohorts, then by abs_log2fc descending.
:::

### Example: HSPA5

<span class="evidence-badge badge-deg">DEG</span> <span class="evidence-badge badge-wgcna">WGCNA</span> <span class="evidence-badge badge-mofa">MOFA</span> <span class="evidence-badge badge-lit">Literature</span>

| Evidence layer | Value |
|---|---|
| DEG consistency | Up in 7/10 cohorts |
| Spearman qP | r = +0.52 |
| Spearman titre | r = +0.38 |
| MOFA Factor 1 weight | +0.392 |
| WGCNA network | network_2_gene (kME = 0.660); ER processing / UPR enriched |
| TF regulators | NFE2L2 (NRF2), FOXO1, PPARA, FOXA1 |
| Literature | PMIDs 32624757, 24081924, 1373378 — GRP78/BiP OE → ↑ titre, ↑ qP |
| **Recommendation** | ▲ **OVEREXPRESS** |

---

## Knockout Candidates

Genes expected to **relieve a productivity bottleneck** when eliminated.

**Criteria:**

- Downregulated in high producers in ≥7/10 cohorts (or upregulated, reflecting a gene that suppresses productivity)
- Negative Spearman correlation with qP (r < −0.5)
- Negative MOFA Factor 1 weight
- Member of an anti-productivity WGCNA network
- Published KO evidence showing positive productivity or quality effect (where available)

::: {.query-box}
Identify knockout candidates: genes with negative MOFA Factor 1 weight, downregulated in ≥7/10 high-producer cohorts, and negative Spearman qP correlation.
:::

### Example: ST14

<span class="evidence-badge badge-deg">DEG</span> <span class="evidence-badge badge-wgcna">WGCNA</span> <span class="evidence-badge badge-mofa">MOFA</span> <span class="evidence-badge badge-lit">Literature</span>

| Evidence layer | Value |
|---|---|
| DEG consistency | Down in 10/10 cohorts |
| Spearman qP | r = −0.51 |
| Spearman titre | r = −0.51 |
| MOFA Factor 1 weight | −0.303 |
| WGCNA network | network_18_gene (kME = 0.595); Cell cycle / DNA replication enriched |
| TF regulators | E2F4 (padj = 3.7×10⁻¹²²), FOXM1, E2F1, MYC |
| Literature | PMID 29777593 — ST14 KO → ↓ fragmentation, ↑ product purity |
| **Recommendation** | ▼ **KNOCKOUT** |

From the 63-gene shortlist, which have concordant RNA–protein regulation — mRNA up and protein up for OE candidates, or mRNA down and protein down for KO candidates?
:::

---

## Molecule-Specific vs. Shared Targets

::: {.query-box}
Compare overexpression candidates between Nivo and C144. Which targets are shared across both molecules, and which are molecule-specific?
:::

Shared targets are preferred for **cell-line-wide** engineering strategies. Molecule-specific targets may address product-specific quality or expression challenges.
